title: Eliminate the access transistor: 1-selector-1-capacitor cross-point decks
idea: Replace the transistor with a two-terminal threshold switch (Mott NbO2 or ovonic chalcogenide) in series with a planar MIM capacitor at every wordline/bitline crossing, stacked in 4-8 decks like cross-point memory; the selector snaps on above Vth to charge/read and blocks below it.
why: Density and capital: 4F2/deck with no epitaxial transistor per tier; trade-off is selector leakage, so targeted as a short-retention (ms) last-level working tier with fast refresh.

title: Two bonded array wafers share one sense-amp plane
idea: Bond two DRAM array wafers face-to-face with the sense-amplifier layer at the bond plane: each SA's true bitline lies in the upper array and its complement in the lower one, combining open-bitline density with folded-bitline noise cancellation because both halves see the same vertical coupling.
why: Periphery (fact 7): one SA row serves two arrays, halving SA area per bit; 4F2-compatible with folded-like margins; ~20-25% die area per bit cut.

title: Invert the supply chain: U.S. makes periphery, bonds arrays
idea: Use the CMOS-bonded-array split to reverse where value sits: periphery wafers come from existing U.S. 28-40 nm logic fabs, array-only wafers come from a lean new U.S. array fab or allied DRAM fabs, and hybrid bonding plus test happen domestically.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital (fact 4): an array-only fab skips ~40% of process steps; underused U.S. mature-node fabs supply periphery; capacity in ~2 years versus 5.

title: Smart-cut tier films with donor-wafer reuse
idea: Worse: consume a full CZ wafer, grown in a Spruce Pine quartz crucible, for every bonded layer and then grind it away. Flip: hydrogen-implant and split a 100-200 nm single-crystal Si film from a donor for each tier, bond it onto the stack, pattern after bonding so alignment is litho-limited, and re-polish and reuse the donor 10-20 times.
why: Single-crystal access transistors in every tier keep the leakage tail low (fact 3) while wafers and crucibles consumed per tier fall ~10-20x (resource chokepoints).

title: Hollow TSVs that are also microfluidic coolant channels
idea: Make annular TSVs whose copper shell carries power/signal while the hollow core carries a two-phase dielectric coolant through the whole stack, combining vertical interconnect and cooling in one via field.
why: Lets compute sit on DRAM (fact 5) while holding DRAM <=60 C; retention roughly doubles per ~10 C, so refresh energy (fact 3) falls 2-4x and 24-32-high stacks become thermally feasible.

title: Ommatidial columns: every vertical bitline gets its own bonded sense amp
idea: As each insect ommatidium wires its photoreceptors to a dedicated neural cartridge, hybrid-bond the 3D array wafer face-to-face to a CMOS wafer at ~0.4 um pitch so every vertical bitline column (64-128 tiers) lands on its own sense amplifier directly beneath, with no global bitlines or column muxes.
why: Periphery 49% and data movement: bitline length equals stack height (~5 um), CBL drops ~10x, periphery leaves the array plane; density +40-60%, read energy ~3x lower.

title: Dsup cloak: grounded coaxial shields wrap each storage node
idea: The tardigrade protein Dsup cloaks DNA against damage; form a grounded TiN sleeve around each vertical storage node with a second conformal ALD liner separated by dielectric, screening neighbour wordlines and sinking carriers injected by repeated activation, which worsen at high temperature.
why: Row hammer and RowPress disturbance grow at 125 C; shielding could raise disturb thresholds ~10x, and the shield-to-node capacitance adds to Cs.

title: Tree rings: concentric ALD shells store three bits per hole
idea: Like growth rings in a trunk, fill one wide high-AR hole with alternating storage and plate shells (TiN/ZrO2/TiN/ZrO2/TiN...). Each storage shell surfaces at a different radius on a terraced top and wires to its own access transistor, so one etched hole holds 2-3 coaxial capacitors.
why: Capacitor wall and litho (facts 1, 4): 2-3x fewer holes per bit; wide holes at relaxed pitch move the critical capacitor litho from EUV to DUV.

title: Minify litho capex: nanoimprint a 4F2 hex array
idea: Commission one $100k nanoimprint master of a hexagonal 4F2 pillar array at about 20 nm pitch and replicate it on coupons with a rented NIL tool, proving pattern fidelity and overlay for the cell layer.
why: Litho capital: one stamp could replace multiple EUV exposures for the regular cell array, about 5-10x cheaper per layer.

title: One-shot epitaxy of stacked GaN electron-gas channel tiers
idea: IFR: 'all tiers grow in one furnace run.' Backward: on sapphire, grow an MOCVD superlattice of 16 AlGaN/GaN heterojunctions, each a 2DEG channel tier with very low off-leakage (3.4 eV gap), then etch gate and storage-node trenches through the stack to form lateral 2DEG gain cells per tier, reusing idle LED/microLED MOCVD fabs.
why: 3D blocker and refresh (facts 2, 3): single-crystal channel tiers with no per-tier deposition or bonding; leakage far below the 13 fA tail.

title: Microfluidic-cooled DRAM tiers keep 32-high stacks at 45 °C
idea: Inverts 'heat must flow down through the stack to one lid.' Etch microchannels into the back side of each thinned DRAM tier and pump dielectric coolant between tiers so retention-critical tiers run ~40 C cooler than in a conventional HBM-style stack.
why: Fact 3: leakage roughly doubles per ~10 C, so ~16x longer retention and much lower refresh power; enables taller stacks.

title: Optane write-off lesson: universal second-life interface on every DRAM die
idea: Intel's Optane exit ended in a large inventory write-down, partly because the dies worked only with one CPU interface. Put a small standardized test-and-reuse port (JTAG-like self-test plus a slow generic protocol) and a wear log on every DRAM die. Dies harvested from retired HBM and DDR modules can then be retested and repackaged into CXL capacity modules.
why: Adds usable supply from retired dies, perhaps 10-20% more bits per year at today's server refresh rates, without new fabs (capital intensity, scarcity).

title: Wavelength-division tier select with color-tuned photoconductive access devices
idea: Scale fiber-optic WDM down to a die: each tier's access device is a photoconductor sensitized by quantum dots of a size unique to that tier, so a waveguide carrying wavelength k turns on only tier k. A tunable laser at the package edge picks the tier in ns, with no staircase or per-tier wordline contacts.
why: Removes the staircase and lateral wordline-driver bottleneck of 3D (fact 2) and part of the periphery (fact 7); tier count is no longer capped by contact area.

title: Bubble-memory bootloop map applied to 3D DRAM strings
idea: Magnetic bubble chips shipped with defective minor loops masked by an on-chip loop map, then died on speed. Give every 3D DRAM die a rewritable defect map at the vertical-string level. Firmware retires defective or worn strings in the field, and the map's health record grades the die for second-life reuse.
why: Tolerating ~5% bad strings brings yield of 26+ tier 3D DRAM (fact 2) to economic levels, extends service life, and makes regrading and reuse possible.

title: Titanium nitride mirror plate pillar serves two cell strings per hole
idea: Lay out 3D DRAM so each vertical TiN plate-line pillar sits between two mirrored lateral cell strings whose capacitors both wrap that same pillar; one deep plate etch and fill serves twice the cells and anchors the alignment of both strings.
why: Halves the deep plate/capacitor holes per bit and recovers ~25% of array footprint in vertical-wordline 3D DRAM (fact 2), cutting critical etch and litho steps (fact 4).

title: Magnify capacitor height with three stacked 40:1 decks
idea: Build the capacitor mold in three decks, each AR about 40 (easy to etch), joined by self-aligned landing plugs, borrowing the multi-deck channel-hole method of 3D NAND. The total effective AR is about 120.
why: Charge wall: reaches the AR about 115 that higher Cs requires using existing etchers. Cs rises about 1.6x, which could relax VARY or extend retention.

title: Cold-side memory: DRAM tiers face the cold plate
idea: IFR: 'memory sits at coolant temperature even on a 1 kW chip.' Backward: flip the 3D stack so DRAM tiers touch the cold plate with logic beneath, and carry logic heat up through dense copper or diamond-like-carbon thermal pillars that pass through dedicated keep-out columns in the array.
why: Refresh (fact 3): retention roughly doubles per 10 C; holding DRAM 30-40 C cooler cuts refresh ~8x and makes memory-on-logic stacking viable.

title: Macronix self-healing flash applied: wordline-heater anneal of DRAM leakage tails
idea: Macronix showed around 2012 that flash cells heal when current through the wordline heats them for milliseconds, but never productized it. In 3D DRAM, pulse current through the metal wordlines during scheduled maintenance to heat cells locally to ~350-400C for microseconds. This anneals the trap sites behind the leakage tail and variable retention time.
why: Shrinks the <=13 fA leakage tail that sets refresh (fact 3), for ~2-4x longer refresh intervals over life. Repair happens in the field.

title: Area-cheap foil cells: planar 8 fF capacitors without high aspect
idea: Fabricate 1T1C arrays roll-to-roll on polyimide by UV nanoimprint at ~1 um features, using a flat 1 um^2 metal/AlOx(10 nm, spatial ALD)/metal capacitor per cell and a printed oxide TFT access device.
why: Cost per area from first principles: processed DRAM wafers cost ~$100k/m^2 versus ~$20-100/m^2 for R2R films, so the area that forces 60-75:1 pillars (fact 1) becomes nearly free; C=eA/d gives ~8 fF on a flat plate, a 10 cm^2/Vs TFT charges it in ~5-10 ns, and one layer holds ~60 GB/m^2.

title: Time-to-threshold sensing on long vertical bitlines
idea: Shift the sense signal from voltage to time: each mat's vertical bitline is precharged and released, and a shared time-to-digital converter measures how many ns it takes to cross a threshold, a delay set by the cell's charge. Integrating over a longer window tolerates 2-3x higher bitline-to-cell capacitance ratios.
why: Lets smaller Cs (fact 1) and taller stacks (fact 2) work; fewer, shared sense circuits shrink the periphery (fact 7).

title: Grounded shield pillars between vertical wordlines trade area for hammer immunity
idea: In vertical-wordline 3D DRAM, substitute every other wordline pillar with a grounded shield pillar etched in the same hole step and tied to the common plate, so no active wordline has an active neighbor; the lost area is bought back with ~30% more tiers, which is cheaper than area in 3D.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): coupling and electron-migration paths terminate on a fixed-potential conductor, expected threshold 1k -> >100k activations, removing TRR/RFM refresh overhead (part of fact 3's 10-20% bandwidth tax).

title: Failed SrTiO3 DRAM capacitors revived with self-clearing electrodes
idea: SrTiO3 (k ~100+) DRAM capacitors were researched and abandoned because weak spots leaked and broke down. Use an ultra-thin top electrode that vaporizes locally around a breakdown site, as in self-healing metallized-film capacitors. Each defect is isolated, so the capacitor loses a tiny area instead of shorting.
why: Delivers the k ~70+ the charge wall calls for (fact 1), allowing lower-AR pillars (AR ~40) while preserving yield. Self-repair is built in.

title: One sense amplifier per vertical stack, multiplexed across 32 tiers
idea: Because only one tier of a bank is activated at a time, give each vertical column of 32 tiers a single sense amplifier reached through a per-tier select transistor at the column foot, instead of one sense amp per bitline per tier.
why: Periphery is ~49% of the die (fact 7): sense-amp area per bit divides by the tier count, pushing periphery toward ~5-10% of footprint and making the 26-tier break-even (fact 2) reachable with cheaper tiers.

title: In-stack binary threshold decoder replaces the 3D staircase
idea: IFR: 'tier selection takes zero area.' Backward: thread 7 vertical select-gate rods through each bitline column and give each tier's series select transistors a binary code of high/low thresholds (set by one coarse i-line implant mask per tier as it is deposited), so a 7-bit voltage pattern on the rods opens only the one tier of 128 whose code matches, an old ROM depletion decoder turned vertical.
why: Periphery (fact 7) and 3D cost (fact 2): deletes the staircase, its contact landings and per-tier wordline drivers, ~10-20% die area at 100+ tiers.

title: Eliminate implant masks: junctionless in-situ doped access channels
idea: Grow channels in-situ doped during epitaxy or deposition and use junctionless accumulation-mode access transistors, removing source/drain and well implant masks with their resist strips and post-implant wet cleans.
why: Water: each implant layer costs resist develop, ash plus wet strip and rinse; removing 6-10 implant layers in the array cuts a major water block and also avoids junction leakage tails.

title: In-situ-doped junctionless channels for buried lateral tiers
idea: Worse: try to implant source/drain into tiers buried 3 um deep where no ion can reach. Flip: dope every channel tier uniformly during epitaxy or deposition and build junctionless gate-all-around access devices that turn off by full depletion, eliminating every per-tier implant and activation anneal.
why: Removes the lateral-transistor doping blocker in 3D DRAM (fact 2) and the dopant-diffusion variability that feeds the leakage tail (fact 3).

title: Sulfur-anchored monolayers enable mask-free self-aligned contacts in stacked tiers
idea: Dip the wafer in an alkanethiol solution so a self-assembled monolayer binds only to exposed Cu lines, then ALD Al2O3 grows only on the dielectric (area-selective deposition); strip the SAM to leave metal exposed and perfectly self-aligned for the next tier's vias.
why: Each self-aligned level removes a critical alignment mask and its overlay budget (fact 4) and allows tighter via pitch in 3D stacks; a thiol bath and ALD are standard university equipment.

title: Thin-film gated thyristor cells stacked in tiers
idea: Shrink the regenerative gain of kiloamp power thyristors to a cell: build gated thin-film p-n-p-n thyristors vertically in each poly-Si tier at 180-nm rules, each acting as both storage element and amplifier. Cells need no capacitor and drive uA read currents into long shared bitlines.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1) and periphery (fact 7): no capacitor, and high read current allows longer bitlines with fewer sense amps.

title: Inside-out flower cell: plate in the hole, transistors radiating
idea: Invert the lateral 3D DRAM cell: each through-stack hole holds a shared plate pillar; the tier's silicon around it is recessed into a ring capacitor, and 4-6 lateral access transistors radiate outward to per-tier horizontal bitlines. Built on a 3D NAND tool line reusing its hole and slit mask types, plus one added plate-contact mask.
why: 3D cell (fact 2) and capacitor (fact 1): each hole serves 4-6 cells per tier with capacitor area growing with hole circumference, roughly doubling bits per hole versus one-cell-per-hole lateral designs.

title: Spatial-ALD nanolaminate replaces Si/SiGe epitaxy for 128 tiers
idea: Under 400 C, deposit 128 alternating 8 nm IGZO (or indium-free ZTO) channel layers and 20 nm AlOx sacrificial layers in one spatial-ALD run, then build lateral 3D DRAM cells by hole/slit recess as in Si/SiGe flows.
why: Fact 2: removes about $5M epi tools and strain limits; tier deposition cost per wafer about 1/5 and tier count is not limited by strain.

title: 77 K re-architected array: longer bitlines, halved wordline voltage
idea: Redesign the array for liquid-nitrogen operation: copper resistivity drops ~5x and subthreshold swing falls to ~15-20 mV/dec, so bitlines can be 2-4x longer with fewer sense amps, Vt can drop ~0.3 V and wordline boost shrinks from ~3 V to ~1.5 V.
why: kT physics: retention grows by many decades (refresh nearly vanishes, fact 3), CV^2 falls ~4x (fact 10) and sense-amp count halves (fact 7); honestly net-positive only after ~10x cryocooler overhead, so it targets large pooled-memory racks.

title: Alternate tiers rotate wordline direction 90 degrees against row hammer
idea: [Box: lateral 1T1C | IGZO lateral FET | standard SA | monolithic 3D tiers | Si | ALD] In a stacked array, tier k runs wordlines along x and tier k+1 along y, so no wordline has a parallel aggressor directly above or below, and in-tier neighbors are separated by grounded shield lines from the same metal.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): vertical parallel coupling disappears, pushing flip thresholds back toward 10k-100k activations and freeing mitigation refresh bandwidth.

title: Hexagonal three-axis lattice: select cells by two of three lines
idea: Inverts 'arrays are square grids addressed by row and column.' Pack vertical pillars in a hexagonal lattice crossed by three line directions at 60 degrees and select a cell by coincidence of any two lines, packing ~13% denser and giving a spare addressing path around a broken line.
why: Fact 4: ~3.5F² effective cell without finer litho, plus built-in redundancy against line defects.

title: Chromatin-style folded thin-film memory sheet stacked by origami
idea: As DNA packs 2 m into a 6 um nucleus by folding, fabricate one long planar oxide-TFT DRAM sheet (a single cheap litho tier) on a releasable 2 um membrane with thinned Miura-ori hinge creases carrying metal traces, then pleat it accordion-style onto the CMOS die so each fold becomes a tier and fold edges land on a bond-pad strip.
why: 3D layer count and capital: N tiers for one tier's lithography and no high-AR stack etch, so array capex per bit falls roughly as 1/N.

title: Minify the 3D demo: 4-tier Si/SiGe cells on 100 mm coupons
idea: Buy commercial Si/SiGe superlattice epitaxy wafers (about $5-10k each), then in a rented university cleanroom selectively remove SiGe, ALD gate and capacitor stacks, and demonstrate a 4-tier lateral-channel 1T1C cell with retention data in 18 months.
why: A credible 3D cell data point that de-risks licensing or fundraising for about $400k, against vendor 3D programs costing billions.

title: Cell layout co-designed with block-copolymer hexagonal lattice
idea: Combine directed self-assembly and the vertical-channel cell: put transistors and capacitors on the natural hexagonal lattice of a cylinder-forming block copolymer, with zig-zag wordlines and 60-degree bitlines matched to that symmetry, so one coarse guide exposure plus self-assembly defines the array.
why: Litho and capital (fact 4): replaces 2-3 EUV layers; hex packing at pitch 2F gives ~3.5F2 per cell versus 6F2 (~40% denser).

title: Wide I/O fixed: thermal-break bond layer under DRAM-on-SoC
idea: JEDEC Wide I/O (DRAM stacked on mobile SoCs) died because SoC hot spots doubled DRAM refresh and because nobody wanted the TSV yield liability. Insert a porous low-k bonding layer with copper pillars that cuts heat flow into the DRAM about 5x. Add refresh zoning driven by a live SoC thermal map, so only rows above hot cores refresh fast.
why: Brings back 3D DRAM-on-logic for data-movement energy (fact 5: from 10-20 pJ/bit to under 1 pJ/bit) while capping refresh overhead (fact 3).

title: Open standard periphery-free array tier any mature fab can build
idea: Inverts 'one company makes the whole DRAM stack.' Publish an open spec for an array-only tier (bond-pad map, electrical rules, materials limited to Si, Al, Ti, N, O and Cu-Mn) so many small fabs supply interchangeable tiers to independent stacking houses.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital intensity: spreads the $15B fab across many existing sites; supplier diversity lowers chokepoint risk.

title: Heat-shock chaperone pulses: wordlines double as micro-heaters that heal devices
idea: Cells survive heat by making heat-shock proteins that refold damaged proteins; in maintenance windows, copy a tier's data away, drive current through its wordline plate as a resistive heater to pulse its access transistors to ~250 C for milliseconds, annealing BTI traps and redistributing hydrogen, then copy the data back.
why: 10 yrs at 125 C drifts Vt (BTI, hydrogen in oxide channels) and collapses retention; periodic in-situ annealing resets aging, potentially extending life 3-5x or shrinking guard-bands.

title: Reverse the plate's role: drop the plate to park idle cells
idea: Segment the capacitor plate per subarray and, when a subarray goes idle, ramp its plate down ~0.3-0.4 V so all floating storage nodes couple down with it; stored '1's then sit at lower field versus the gate/junction (less GIDL and trap-assisted leakage) while '0's sit slightly below ground held off by the negative back-bias. The plate ramps back up before the next activation, restoring the levels.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): GIDL/TAT leakage is exponential in field, so a 0.3-0.4 V reduction could cut tail leakage 3-10x, stretching refresh intervals and cutting the 16-33% idle refresh power proportionally.

title: Spin-qubit plasma-free fab: vapor-HCl carved lateral cells in Si/SiGe
idea: Silicon spin-qubit fabs avoid plasma damage; grow 3D DRAM tiers as an epitaxial Si/SiGe superlattice in H2 carrier, open vertical slits by metal-assisted wet etch, then remove the SiGe selectively with gas-phase HCl to open lateral cavities where gate and capacitor stacks are deposited by ALD. No plasma ever touches the channel.
why: Lateral 3D DRAM transistor quality (fact 2): damage-free channels cut trap-assisted leakage tail (fact 3) ~3-10x, with no argon.

title: Retool idle 3D-NAND channel-hole lines into oxide gain-cell strings
idea: Shift the time horizon to the NAND glut cycle: 3D-NAND fabs already etch 200+ tier channel holes and staircases. Swap the charge-trap ONO for an ALD oxide-semiconductor channel and use the word-plane stack as write and read gates of 2T0C gain cells strung vertically, so existing $10B+ lines can run DRAM-class memory during NAND downturns.
why: Capital intensity and 3-5-year fab lead times (fact 4): converts existing tier-stacking capacity to DRAM-class memory in ~12-18 months.

title: Magnify row spacing: spend 3D density on grounded shield wordlines
idea: In a stacked array where density is abundant, insert a grounded shield wordline between every pair of active wordlines and a shield plane between tiers, so aggressor-victim capacitive and charge-migration coupling falls sharply.
why: Row hammer: the flip threshold could rise from about 1k to about 100k activations, removing costly TRR and RFM overheads for about 30% of area.

title: Polycrystalline diamond bond layer doubles as interlayer heat spreader
idea: Combine bonding dielectric and heat spreader: grow ~1 um CVD diamond (US-built reactors, methane/hydrogen feedstock) on DRAM wafers, polish it, and use it as the bond layer between a hot logic die and DRAM tiers so hotspots spread laterally before reaching the cells.
why: Enables logic-on-DRAM stacking (fact 5) while keeping DRAM below 85 C (refresh doubles per ~10 C, fact 3); diamond ~1,000 W/mK versus 1.4 for SiO2; all-domestic inputs.

title: BiFeO3 exchange-coupled magnetoelectric tiers via layer transfer
idea: Magnetoelectric exchange coupling: about 100 mV across La-doped BiFeO3 rotates its antiferromagnetic order, which flips an exchange-coupled CoFe magnet read by an MTJ. The BFO is grown at high temperature on donor wafers, then layer-transferred into stacked BEOL tiers.
why: Gives non-volatile bits at sub-volt write voltage (fact 10) with stackable tiers (fact 2); claim aJ-level writes, 10-30x below DRAM CV2.

title: Electroforming bath: superconformal cobalt fill replaces CVD tungsten wordlines
idea: Jewelry electroforming fills molds bottom-up; use suppressor/accelerator plating chemistry for bottom-up cobalt or copper fill of buried wordlines and 3D lateral wordline recesses on existing plating tools, dropping CVD tungsten.
why: Removes a ~80% China-sourced tungsten dependency and lowers wordline resistance ~2-3x, allowing longer wordlines and fewer drivers (fact 7).

title: Interference-printed array: zero EUV inside the cell field
idea: IFR: 'the array needs no masks at all.' Backward: because the cell field is perfectly periodic, print it with two-beam 193 nm immersion interference (~76 nm pitch) plus spacer quadruple/octuple patterning to ~19/10 nm, with crossed exposures for pillars, and reserve projection or EUV litho for mat edges and periphery only.
why: Litho capital (fact 4): 5-7 EUV array layers drop to ~1-2 total, cutting the ~55% depreciation share of wafer cost by roughly a quarter.

title: Square-meter memory from idle Gen-10.5 LCD panel fabs
idea: IFR: 'the fab already exists and costs nothing new.' Backward: run 8 stacked tiers of 2T0C oxide-semiconductor gain cells at ~1 um rules on 2.9 x 3.4 m LCD glass panels in under-used display fabs, accepting ~100x lower areal density because processed panel area costs hundreds of dollars per m2 versus tens of thousands for DRAM wafers.
why: Capital and cost per bit (fact 4): ~50-100 GB/m2 at roughly $5-10/GB with no new fab, as a 50-100 ns far-memory tier that offloads DRAM demand.

title: Charge-modulated bipolar gain cell from a 1990s BiCMOS line
idea: Scale the signal up by gain instead of capacitor size: store charge on the floating base of a vertical bipolar transistor stacked over the access device, so read current is ~beta (about 100) times what the stored charge alone would give. A ~0.5-fF node yields the read signal of a ~50-fF capacitor.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): 100x current gain stands in for capacitor size, on depreciated 0.35-0.25 um BiCMOS lines.

title: Bitlines on the wafer backside for vertical-transistor 4F2 DRAM
idea: TRIZ #13 The other way round: build vertical transistors and capacitors from the front, then flip, thin and form bitlines from the back so they land directly on pillar bottoms, as backside power delivery does in logic. This replaces the high-resistance buried bitline under the pillars.
why: Fact 4: removes the hardest step of 4F2 vertical-channel DRAM; ~5x lower bitline resistance allows longer bitlines and a 33% smaller cell than 6F2.

title: Skyscraper sky lobby: sense-amp tier every 16 cell tiers
idea: Like express elevators that feed sky lobbies, a 128-tier vertical-bitline 3D DRAM inserts a layer-transferred single-crystal Si sense-amp tier every 16 cell tiers. Each local vertical bitline spans only 16 cells, and sensed data rides 'express' global vertical lines down to the base die.
why: 3D blocker (fact 2) and capacitor wall (fact 1): bitline capacitance per sense ~8x lower, so a 1-1.5 fF lateral capacitor gives the signal of today's 5 fF pillar, which makes lateral 3D capacitors good enough.

title: Hard-disk TDMR: joint bitline sensing cancels neighbor crosstalk
idea: Adapted from two-dimensional magnetic recording, where multiple readers cancel inter-track interference: sense amps resolve neighboring bitline pairs jointly and subtract a calibrated coupling term, letting bitline pitch go below today's coupling limit.
why: Bitline pitch ~25-30% tighter at the same litho (fact 4), cost per bit ~-20%, and tolerance for denser 3D pitches.

title: Eliminate the common plate: pairwise differential plateless capacitors
idea: Remove the shared top-plate electrode and its conformal TiN/poly fill; neighbouring pillar storage nodes face each other through the high-k film so each pair forms one capacitor written with complementary charge (+Q/-Q) and read differentially on a folded bitline pair.
why: Capacitor charge wall: differential read roughly doubles signal per unit Cs, so ~5 fF pillars behave like ~9-10 fF single-ended; deletes the plate deposition/etch module.

title: 300-layer NAND edge case: area-selective ALD molybdenum wordlines
idea: The tallest 3D NAND stacks already fill wordlines by CVD; take this further for 3D DRAM tiers with area-selective ALD molybdenum (MoCl5/H2 with nitrogen purge) that nucleates only on exposed seed edges in recessed lateral cavities while a self-assembled inhibitor blocks the oxide. No argon-sputtered liner, no tungsten and no wordline-isolation patterning step.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) and argon PVD; void-free low-resistance lateral wordlines allow thinner tiers and more of them (fact 2).

title: Minify staircase contacts: in-tier pass-gate decoders
idea: Build log2(N) pass-gate decoder trees from the same lateral access transistors inside each 3D tier, so the staircase needs about log2 of the per-tier wordline contacts instead of one per row. Validate with TCAD, a 4-tier coupon and a patent package, then license.
why: 3D DRAM blocker: staircase and contact area per tier could fall about 10x, lowering the 26-tier break-even point. Design plus coupon costs about $600k.

title: Thin-film Peltier bonding layer chills DRAM tiers above logic
idea: Peltier effect: a Bi2Te3/Sb2Te3 superlattice thermoelectric layer in the bonding stack between logic and DRAM tiers actively pumps heat downward and doubles as a power-distribution plane. The DRAM tiers stay 20-30 K cooler than the logic.
why: Leakage roughly halves per ~10 K, which attacks refresh (fact 3) and makes memory-on-logic 3D possible; claim 4-8x longer retention, net of Peltier power.

title: Volumetric holographic exposure patterns thirty tiers at once
idea: Worse: expose, develop and etch each tier separately. Flip: spin a thick (3-5 um) photo-patternable hybrid dielectric, write a 3D holographic interference intensity pattern that cross-links the cavity layout of ~30 tiers in one exposure, develop it into a 3D scaffold, then fill the cavities with ALD channel, high-k and metal.
why: One exposure replaces dozens of patterning steps: three exposures for ~90 tiers give ~10x density at roughly today's lithography budget, with no EUV (fact 4).

title: Area-selective ALD self-aligns storage-node landing pads, deleting masks
idea: Combine area-selective deposition with the landing-pad step: inhibitor molecules adsorb on dielectric but not on contact plugs, so Mo/TiN grows only on plugs and mushrooms into self-aligned landing pads on US ALD tools, removing the landing-pad lithography.
why: Fact 4: deletes one of the 5-7 EUV layers and an overlay-critical step (~5-8% wafer cost), making a non-EUV US flow more viable.

title: Tin-copper solid-liquid interdiffusion bonds stack tiers without remelting earlier joints
idea: Bond each memory tier with thin Sn on Cu pads at ~250 C; the Sn fully converts to Cu3Sn/Cu6Sn5 intermetallic that melts above ~600 C, so later bonding steps never reflow earlier joints, allowing sequential 8-16-high stacks on a simple flip-chip bonder.
why: A low-cost, particle-tolerant alternative to hybrid bonding for stacked memory (fact 6) using abundant Sn and Cu, buildable in university packaging labs.

title: Core-style low selection ratio crosspoint that accepts and scrubs disturbs
idea: Core memory lived with a 2:1 selection ratio; build a 16-deck passive crosspoint of plain ferroelectric capacitors driven by a simple V/2 scheme, let each write flip up to 1% of half-selected cells, and have a write-then-scrub engine sweep the touched lines with a strong code before errors accumulate.
why: Facts 2 and 7: drops selectors and multi-level V/3 drivers (simpler periphery), enabling 16 decks of transistor-free cells at an effective ~0.25F2 per bit.

title: Haversian canals: copper heat channels keep a hot stack isothermal
idea: Bone threads Haversian canals through dense tissue to serve deep cells; run Cu-filled canal pillars through dummy columns of the 3D array every ~20 um, linking each tier to the heat spreader, so a 100-tier stack over logic adds <3 C above a 125 C ambient instead of ~15 C.
why: Keeps junctions inside the 125 C envelope for 10 years (each +10 C roughly halves retention and EM/TDDB life), enabling DRAM-on-logic stacking at automotive grade.

title: Honeycomb-core expansion: staggered-anchor films stretch into capacitor walls
idea: Aerospace honeycomb is made by gluing stacked sheets in staggered stripes and pulling them apart; analogously deposit thin metal/dielectric sheets separated by sacrificial layers with staggered anchor stripes, release them, and let programmed stress expand the stack vertically into a hexagonal wall array that becomes shared capacitor plates.
why: Creates tall capacitor walls with no high-AR etch (facts 1, 4), potentially >100:1 effective aspect ratio for the cost of planar deposition; speculative because nanoscale expansion must be uniform across the wafer.

title: Silicon carbide vertical 4F2 cells for near-refresh-free retention
idea: Build vertical-channel 4F2 cells in 4H-SiC (3.3 eV gap) on the 200 mm SiC wafer base scaled for EV power devices: implanted buried n+ bitlines, trench gate-all-around channels and a stacked capacitor on top, where intrinsic carrier density ~1e-9 cm^-3 suppresses junction and GIDL leakage by >1e8 vs Si.
why: Attacks the leakage tail (fact 3), aiming at minutes of retention so refresh power and bandwidth loss vanish, while tapping a US-anchored substrate and tool base outside the DRAM supply chain.

title: Ball-bearing packing: colloidal monolayer masks for hex vertical-channel arrays
idea: Like ball bearings settling in a tray, float a Langmuir monolayer of 40-60 nm silica spheres onto wafers, shrink them in plasma to set hole size, and etch a hexagonal vertical-channel array with mature etch tools; periphery uses ordinary litho and colloid grain boundaries are mapped out as spare rows.
why: Dense hex arrays at ~50 nm pitch without immersion or EUV (fact 4); at roughly a quarter of leading-edge wafer cost, cost per bit approaches mainstream for capacity memory.

title: Newspaper-press memory: IGZO DRAM arrays in idle LCD panel fabs
idea: Like a newspaper press trading resolution for acreage, run 2T0C/1T1C IGZO arrays at ~1 um rules on Gen-6/8.5 glass in under-used LCD and LTPS fabs, dice them into memory tiles and pair them with small CMOS controller chiplets as a CXL capacity tier.
why: At ~4 um2/bit a Gen-8.5 panel holds ~170 GB per layer; at ~$500-1000 per processed panel that is ~$3-6/GB with no new fab; IGZO's low leakage eases refresh, but access will be ~100 ns-class.

title: ReRAM endurance failure fixed: strippable, re-coatable consumable memory layer
idea: ReRAM and PCM never replaced DRAM partly because the switching film wears out. Put the switching film as the top BEOL layer over a permanent CMOS base die, designed so a depot can plasma-strip and redeposit it. A worn die is then remanufactured instead of scrapped.
why: Lets cheap BEOL memories do DRAM's job despite finite endurance, while the expensive CMOS base (periphery, fact 7) is reused 3-5 times.

title: Chessboard: alternating NMOS and PMOS access rows neutralize row hammer
idea: Black and white squares alternate: alternate n-channel and p-channel access transistors (storing opposite logic polarity) row by row, so an aggressor's wordline swings opposite to its neighbors' turn-on polarity. Its capacitive kick pushes the victims further off, and the electron-injection mechanism behind hammer flips works against p-type neighbors.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): aiming at a >10x higher flip threshold (1k to 10k+ activations); coupling is cancelled at the source rather than mitigated by refresh logic.

title: Minify the fab: iterate 3D tiers on half-inch-wafer tools
idea: Rent time on half-inch-wafer minimal-fab tool sets, about 1/1000 the capex of a 300 mm line with cycle times of days, to run hundreds of 3D DRAM tier process splits (deposition, selective recess, ALD) in 24 months.
why: Capital and time: turns 3D cell R&D from a $100M problem into a budget below $1M, with 10x more learning cycles.

title: Mixed-use zoning: a compute tier after every eight memory tiers
idea: Copy urban mixed-use zoning into monolithic 3D: add a thin-film logic tier (adders, popcount, comparators) after every 8 memory tiers, so reductions happen within ~1 um of the data and only results travel down the stack.
why: Data-movement energy (fact 5): moving a bit 1 um costs fJ, versus pJ to reach HBM; targets 10-30x less energy for reduction-heavy AI kernels.

title: Thermal-cycling satellite stack with doped-silicon vias, no copper or tungsten
idea: Satellites cycle -150 to +120 C and copper vias crack silicon through CTE mismatch; build through-tier and through-die vias from degenerately doped epitaxial or poly silicon and fusion-bond Si to Si, so the whole stack is one CTE-matched material. Vias are fat but short because tiers are thinned to a few um.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) from vias and Cu-pumping keep-out zones, shrinking the TSV area tax (fact 6) ~2x and raising stack reliability.

title: Vertical charge-coupled columns store packets without access transistors
idea: Deposit a 3D-NAND-like gate stack around a single-crystal or recrystallized channel and clock the gate tiers in three phases to shift charge packets up the column to one sense node at the top, so 128 bits share one transistor and no capacitor.
why: Leakage physics: a buried potential well loses charge only by thermal generation, far below a transistor off-state tail (fact 3), and removing the per-cell capacitor sidesteps the charge wall (fact 1); a 128-deep shift at ~1 ns per step keeps access near DRAM class while density follows tier count.

title: Veneer-peel tiers: spall device layers instead of grinding wafers away
idea: Veneer mills peel thin sheets from a log instead of sawing it; after front-end processing on mature lines, deposit a stressed nickel layer and controlled-spall the top 10-20 um device layer for stacking, then repolish and reuse the parent substrate 5-10 times.
why: Backgrinding for stacking discards ~97% of each wafer; spalling cuts wafer and Spruce Pine crucible consumption per stacked tier ~5x and makes thin tiers with only a spall station added.

title: Iron-nickel magnetic pads self-align dies for fine-pitch hybrid bonding
idea: Pattern soft-magnetic FeNi pads at die corners and matching hard-magnetic pads on the target wafer; dies placed by a coarse pick-and-place onto a thin water film self-register to <200 nm via magnetic plus capillary forces before Cu/SiCN hybrid bonding.
why: Die-to-wafer bonding throughput and aligner capital choke HBM stacking (fact 6); magnetic self-assembly could run ~10x faster on cheaper tools, enabling known-good-die stacks with fewer TSV-heavy wafer stacks.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching drills 300-tier holes without plasma
idea: Worse: push million-dollar cryogenic plasma etchers past 75:1 one wafer at a time. Flip: pattern a thin Au/Ag catalyst mesh and let metal-assisted chemical etching (HF/H2O2) sink it straight down through a Si/SiGe superlattice in a wet batch bath, producing holes and slits at AR >200 for ~300 tiers.
why: Etch aspect ratio stops capping tier count (facts 2, 4) and a batch wet step costs a fraction of plasma etch, so a 300-tier stack lands near today's wafer cost; at ~60F2 per tier-cell that is ~30 nm2/bit, comfortably >10x.

title: Roof shingles: inclined lateral capacitors overlap neighbor footprints
idea: Like overlapping roof shingles, each lateral capacitor in a 3D stack is built on a slant, climbing one tier over its length, so it extends beneath the next cell's footprint without colliding; the slant comes from an inclined sacrificial ramp cut by tilted ion-beam etch.
why: Doubles capacitor length per lateral pitch in 3D DRAM (facts 1-2), ~2x Cs without raising tier pitch.

title: Capacitor-boosted 2T1C gain cell for thin lateral 3D tiers
idea: In each lateral 3D tier, combine a 0.5-1 fF short horizontal capacitor with a separate read transistor whose gate is the storage node; the capacitor only has to hold that gate's charge between refreshes, not drive a bitline.
why: Charge wall and 3D blocker (facts 1-2): lateral capacitors 5-10x shorter, tiers ~40 nm thick so 100+ tiers are plausible; read is nondestructive (fact 8).

title: Coolant-in-substrate microchannel glass keeps stacked memory tiers cold
idea: IFR: 'heat never reaches the memory.' Backward: fuse two glass sheets with etched microfluidic channels into the substrate itself, build oxide memory tiers directly on top, and pump coolant 50 um below the cells so memory placed under a hot accelerator stays near 30 C.
why: Refresh and data movement (facts 3, 5): memory can sit directly beneath compute; leakage halves every ~10 C, cutting refresh ~8x.

title: Saturn-V voting plus Whirlwind marginal checking per tier band
idea: Revive Whirlwind's marginal checking (stressing voltages to expose weak parts) and the Saturn V LVDC's triple voting: at boot and periodically the controller lowers array voltage per tier band to measure margin, then runs strong tiers raw at up to 1% cell BER under the normal code and weak top/bottom tiers in 3-way voted mode.
why: Fact 2: no tier is discarded, so a 128-tier stack with uneven etch still yields; density loss <10% versus scrapping wafers.

title: Pitch-for-tiers trade: 200-tier DRAM on depreciated DUV fabs
idea: Worse: chase F~12 nm with 5-7 EUV layers on new, fully depreciating tools. Flip: relax the lateral pitch to F~20 nm, which DUV immersion SAQP prints in already-depreciated logic or NAND fabs, and buy density back with ~200 tiers whose added cost is only deposition and a shared etch.
why: A ~40F2 lateral cell at F=20 nm is 16,000 nm2 per tier, so 200 tiers give ~80 nm2/bit (~11x versus 6F2 at 12 nm); with depreciation (~55% of wafer cost, fact 4) mostly gone and no EUV, wafer cost holds flat despite the extra deposition.

title: Minify litho to zero EUV: block-copolymer hex-lattice 4F2
idea: Let block-copolymer cylinders self-assemble into a hexagonal lattice at about 24 nm pitch, guided by one coarse DUV template, to define the vertical-channel pillars and caps of a hexagonal 4F2 array.
why: Litho capital: could replace 3-5 EUV layers with a spin-coat and bake, cutting array patterning cost about 5x.

title: Woven wordlines zig-zag between tier pairs like weft threads
idea: Treat wordlines as weft threads: each lateral wordline hops between tier k and k+1 every 32 cells through short vias while its partner runs in the opposite phase, so a raised wordline opens a checkerboard row spanning both tiers. Address logic maps it as one logical row, so one staircase contact serves two tiers and systematic tier-thickness variation averages out.
why: 3D staircase area and tier variability (facts 2, 7): halves staircase contacts and their decoder footprint; claims ~2x shorter staircase region and a tighter access-transistor Vt distribution.

title: Hexagonal vertical bitlines with three cells radiating per tier
idea: Worse: use square grids where each vertical bitline serves cells in only two directions, wasting footprint between capacitors. Flip: place vertical bitlines on a hexagonal lattice with lateral cells radiating at 120 degrees and wordline planes cut into three interleaved phases, so each bitline serves three cells per tier.
why: ~1.4-1.5x cells per footprint per tier in lateral 3D DRAM, i.e., ~30% fewer tiers to hit the 26-tier break-even (fact 2).

title: Minify die to 4 um thick: 64-high nano-TSV stack
idea: Use wafer-on-wafer bonding and grind each DRAM wafer to an etch stop at about 4 um, then link layers with 0.5 um nano-TSVs instead of 40 um microbumps, stacking 64 dies in about 300 um.
why: HBM TSV tax: TSV keep-out area could fall 10-50x and stack height capacity rise 4-5x.

title: Pyroelectric tile sensors steer per-tile refresh in memory-on-logic stacks
idea: Pyroelectric effect: a thin HZO pyroelectric sheet in each tier's bonding layer outputs charge proportional to dT/dt over ~1 mm2 tiles, driving an analog integrator that sets each tile's refresh interval directly without ADCs or thermal diodes. Cool tiles refresh at 256 ms while only hot tiles above logic hot spots stay at 32-64 ms.
why: Attacks refresh energy and bandwidth loss (fact 3) that grows when DRAM tiers sit on hot logic in 3D; claim 2-4x less refresh than worst-case whole-die timing.

title: Molybdenum-dioxide electrodes template rutile TiO2 for short lateral capacitors
idea: Combine a rutile-structured MoO2 storage electrode (from Colorado molybdenum) with ALD TiO2 so the dielectric grows in its rutile phase (k ~80-100) below 400 C, with light Al doping to curb leakage, replacing imported Ru/RuO2 templates and k~40 ZrO2.
why: Charge wall (fact 1, needs k~70): ~2x k makes lateral 3D capacitors ~2x shorter for thinner tiers; element chain Mo/Ti/Al is fully domestic.

title: Eliminate water rinses: supercritical CO2 cleaning of capacitor holes
idea: Replace post-etch wet cleans and IPA drying of high-AR capacitor holes with supercritical CO2 plus co-solvent cleaning and drying in one chamber, so no liquid-vapour meniscus ever forms inside the structures.
why: Water: removes the UPW rinses of the capacitor module, the most rinse-heavy part of the cell. Removing capillary collapse also unlocks the AR ~115:1 needed to break the charge wall.

title: Wordline drivers built on the 3D staircase steps
idea: Combine the 3D contact staircase with the X-decoder: deposit thin-film transistors directly on each staircase tread so every tier's wordline driver and pre-decoder sits on its own step, turning dead staircase area into periphery.
why: Periphery (fact 7) and 3D cost (fact 2): removes decoder strips and long fan-out wires; ~8-12% die area recovered.

title: Librarian's bookshelf: memory dies standing upright on logic
idea: The librarian stores books on edge, not in flat piles. Stand 50 um thinned memory dies upright on a logic die, joined through half-via castellations made by dicing through plated vias at the die edge and soldered to the base. Coolant or air flows between the dies.
why: ~20 dies per mm of base. No TSVs and no stack-height thermal penalty (Fact 6). Dicing, plating and reflow are small-team tools.

title: One mandrel, eight spacers, punched through 32 tiers
idea: Amortize one sub-litho pattern across many tiers: print 180-nm mandrel lines with KrF, run three rounds of sidewall-spacer doubling to reach ~22-nm lines, and transfer that pattern once through a 32-tier stack. One patterning sequence serves 32 tiers, so litho cost per bit falls ~32x.
why: Litho capital and EUV dependence (fact 4): sub-25-nm pitch from 1990s steppers, amortized across tiers.

title: Bird-lung one-way flow: every restore goes to a fresh row
idea: Birds ventilate unidirectionally instead of tidally; likewise, after a destructive read the sense amps write the page into a different spare row in the same subarray (tracked by a small per-subarray remap table), so data flows through rows rather than being restored in place and the vacated row becomes the next spare.
why: Row hammer and destructive read: no physical row is activated repeatedly in place because the aggressor keeps moving, restore cost is unchanged, and churn wear-levels; aims at RH immunity without counters.

title: Buckled nanobeam bistable cells stacked in mechanical tiers
idea: Po: the bit is a shape, not a charge. Each cell is a pre-compressed 200 nm single-crystal Si nanobeam in a sealed cavity that buckles up or down; electrodes above and below snap it in ~10 ns and readout senses the capacitance difference, holding state with zero energy, and cavity tiers stack as bonded MEMS layers.
why: Zero refresh and standby; wear-free if strain stays elastic (<0.5% in single-crystal Si). Modest density aimed at a warm-data tier.

title: Negative-capacitance HZO stack gives planar tier capacitors k~70
idea: Ferroelectric negative capacitance: an HZO/ZrO2/Al2O3 superlattice is tuned so the ferroelectric layer sits in a stabilized negative-capacitance regime, raising the series stack's effective permittivity toward k~70. Each tier can then use short lateral planar capacitors instead of AR 60-75 pillars.
why: Hits the k~70 escape route from the capacitor wall (fact 1) and lets 3D tiers shrink (fact 2); claim 2-3x Cs per area and ~40% thinner tier pitch.

title: Minify bitline noise: helical twisted bitlines across tiers
idea: In a 3D vertical-bitline array, route bitline pairs so they swap tier positions every 16 cells, forming a helix that cancels BL-BL coupling noise. Prove it with SPICE and extracted parasitics plus a small 130 nm MPW test array.
why: Charge wall: lower noise lets sense margin, and so Cs, shrink by about 20-30%. A design-only path licenses it for under $400k.

title: Burdock-burr walker's velcro: copper nanowire room-temperature stack bonding
idea: Velcro came from burrs caught on a walker's clothes. Electroplate copper nanowire forests through track-etched polymer membrane templates on both bonding faces, then press them together at ~10 MPa so the wires interpenetrate into electrical and mechanical joints at room temperature.
why: Stacks memory on logic without nm-flat CMP, a high-temperature anneal or a precision bonder (Fact 6). A 10-person team can do it with plating and a press.

title: Nanotube-forest growth: grow vertical channels instead of etching holes
idea: Adapted from carbon-nanotube forest growth, where catalyst dots sprout aligned tubes millimeters tall: place catalyst at cell sites, grow vertical Si or oxide-semiconductor nanowires to ~5 um by VLS, then build the tier stack around them with low-temperature conformal fills, so no 70:1 hole etch is ever needed.
why: High-AR hole etch and its tools are among the costliest 3D steps (facts 2,4); 100-wafer growth batches cut this module ~50x; misaligned wires handled by redundancy.

title: Backside-etched capacitors in the thinned bulk replace front-side cylinders
idea: Substitute the front-side capacitor stack with capacitors etched from the wafer backside: after front-end transistors and bitlines, bond face-down, thin to ~3 um and etch capacitor holes from the back into silicon directly beneath each access transistor's storage junction, then line with ALD dielectric/electrode.
why: Capacitor charge wall and layout (facts 1, 4): the capacitor no longer competes with bitline/contacts for front area, can use the full 4F² footprint (~1.5x cross-section), and frees the BEOL; Cs ~7-8 fF at today's AR.
